sections.heading: Game Duration
items: Each match is played to 11 points OR up to 10 minutes, whichever comes first.
If tied after 10 minutes, next point wins.

sections.heading: Possession
items: It’s “make-it, take-it” — the player who scores retains possession for the next play.
Ball must be checked to start every possession.
Defender must be inside the 3pt line when checking the ball with a pass.  Offensive player must receive the ball in a standing position directly behind the 3pt line.
Defense gets possession on any jump ball scenario (tie up, ball stuck, referee doesnt know who it was out on).

sections.heading: Clock
items: The game uses a running clock (clock doesn’t stop).

sections.heading: Shot Clock
items: A 7-second shot clock is used on every possession to keep pace fast.
If the ball is deflected out of bounds, the shot clock will not reset and must be rechecked above the 3pt line.

sections.heading: Traditional scoring applies
items: Receive 1 free throw for fouls on a made basket

sections.heading: Fouls
items: Unlimited personal fouls: Players keep playing even after multiple fouls.
Shooting Fouls: When fouled on a shot, the player gets one free throw worth the value of the attempted shot.
Consecutive Non-Shooting Fouls: If a defender commits consecutive non-shooting fouls in the same 7 second possession, the offensive player gets one point AND possession.

sections.heading: Other
items: If a referee deems a player is stalling between possessions he may give a warning and award 1pt for every warning thereafter.
In the Semifinals and Finals, players get one 30 second timeout.  They can only be used between possessions during a dead ball.
